PullRequest.Title: Chat: onboarding spotlight tour for the Copilot harness chat input
PullRequest.Body:
Adds an onboarding spotlight tour of the editor Chat input for new users of **Copilot harness** chats. It reuses the onboarding engine and spotlight primitives from the Agents window tours (`workbench/contrib/onboarding`).

## Behavior
The tour can run when all of these are true:
- The `onb.chatInput` onboarding experiment shows it, or `onboarding.developerMode` previews `chat.onboarding.chatInput`.
- The Chat view shows a Copilot harness chat. The `chat.defaultToCopilotHarness` experiment makes that harness the default.
- The user has never sent an editor chat message.

It has three steps, each described in no more than two short sentences:
1. **Model picker.** Switch models to balance reasoning and cost.
2. **Agent mode.** Opens the mode and permissions picker on its **Agent mode** section (Interactive / Plan / Autopilot).
3. **Permissions.** The menu stays open. Agent mode collapses, and after a short pause the **Permissions** section expands.

The tour runs at most once per user. It is hidden when AI features are disabled (`ChatContextKeys.enabled`), does not start while a modal editor is open, and ends if one opens. Local harness chats never show it.

## Implementation
- **`chatOnboardingEligibility.ts`:** `ChatOnboardingEligibility.eligibleChat` is the visible Chat view showing a Copilot harness chat, when the user has never sent an editor chat message (the existing `EditorChatUsage` counter). It follows session switches and becomes ineligible once the user sends a message. It is separate from the tour UI.
- **`chatInputSpotlightTour.ts`:** the tour scenario, its target providers, and the workbench contribution.
  - The scenario declares `experiment: { behaviorFlag: 'onb.chatInput.show', assignmentContextIdFlag: 'onb.chatInput.id' }`, so the engine gates it and attaches the `onb-` assignment context from the moment the tour would show, in every arm.
  - Its trigger is true only while the chat whose targets rendered is still eligible.
  - It joins its own run through `runScenario` so that a modal editor opening over it ends the tour.
- **`AgentHostChatInputPicker`:** owns the section switching. `showSection(section, token)` opens the menu on a section, or, if the combined menu is already open, collapses the other section and expands this one after a pause. `menuElement` returns the open menu. `ChatInputPart.getAgentHostPicker` returns a narrow view of the mode or permissions picker and drops disposed pickers. The model step uses the existing `getModelPickerControl()`.
- **Onboarding engine:**
  - `IOnboardingTarget.additionalElements` (opt-in) highlights other elements with the target, such as the menu the mode button opens outside itself. The highlight covers them all, clicking the callout keeps focus in them so a menu that closes on blur stays open, Escape inside them is left to them, and the step is announced to screen readers because focus can move into them.
  - `IOnboardingTarget.open` receives the step's cancellation token, so work started by `open` stops when the step ends.
  - An automatic run that waited behind another presentation only starts if its `when` and trigger still hold. Otherwise it is dropped without being marked shown. This applies to every tour.
  - **Unresolved experiment flags are read again on refetch.** The engine still reads a scenario's two treatment flags at startup. While they are unresolved, it reads them again on every `IAssignmentService.onDidRefetchAssignments`, which tas-client fires when a fetch replaces its assignments. That includes the first fetch from the GitHub Copilot ExP endpoint, which VS Code only learns from the signed-in account's entitlements after startup; before that, flags from that workspace read as `undefined`. Once both flags resolve, the arm is fixed for the window. A refetch during a read in flight reads again after that read settles. No timers.

### Caveat on the "never chatted" signal
`chat.editorUsage.messages` has only been recorded since #336792 (about Sept 18). Users who chatted before then look new until they send their next message.

### ExP experiment
[Chat: Onboarding tour for new Copilot harness users](https://exp.microsoft.com/features/017abc8a-cc42-4568-a251-0d67580d7956/progressions?workspaceId=32f04c18-9eb4-4584-a81d-eef352ba43c1) in the GitHub Copilot ExP workspace (`githubdevdiv~vscodecopilotchat`), assigned by `devdeviceid`. It moved from the legacy `vscodeexpws` workspace, where the old feature is now archived. Both experiments are created but **not started**. Start them after a Stable build with this change ships.

| Progression | Variants (`onb.chatInput.show`) | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| A/A: no tour vs no tour | `onb-chat-input-aa-a` (control, `false`) / `onb-chat-input-aa-b` (`false`) | 5% / 5% |
| A/B: no tour vs spotlight tour | `onb-chat-input-ab-none` (control, `false`) / `onb-chat-input-ab-spotlight` (`true`) | 5% / 5% → 10% / 10% → 50% / 50% |
- Each variant sets `onb.chatInput.id` to its own variant id. The engine requires the `onb-` prefix and keeps the assignment context out of telemetry until the user reaches the tour, so no separate trigger event is needed. Scorecards compare the `onb-chat-input-*` assignment contexts.
- **Audience (both):** `extensionname IN ("vscode-core", "github.copilot-chat"); vscode_core_appversion >= 1.142.0; vscode_core_targetpopulation IN ("public"); vscode_core_windowkind IN ("editor")`. Raise `vscode_core_appversion` if this ships later than 1.142.
- **Signed-out users:** this workspace is served only once the user is signed in, because VS Code learns its endpoint from the account. Signed-out users get no assignment and no tour.
- **Traffic:** both progressions share the feature's isolation group, so running experiments can use at most 100% of traffic together. Stop the A/A before the A/B moves to 50% / 50%.

## Validation
- **Unit tests:**
  - `chatInputSpotlightTour.test.ts`: readiness, targets, the experiment, combined and separate permission pickers, the step token reaching the picker, losing eligibility, and ending on a modal editor.
  - `chatOnboardingEligibility.test.ts`: harness, visibility, session switches, the new-user check and bypass, and sending a message.
  - `agentHostChatInputPicker.test.ts`: `showSection` opening a section, moving between sections, ignoring a cancelled request, and handing off between separate pickers.
  - `onboardingService.test.ts`: a queued automatic run that is no longer eligible is dropped without being marked shown, unresolved experiment flags are read again when assignments are refetched and then kept, and a refetch during a read in flight is not missed.
  - `spotlightOverlay.test.ts`: highlighting additional elements, keeping focus in them, and leaving Escape and Tab inside them to them.
  - The existing onboarding, picker, and Agents window tour tests pass.
- **Checks:** `typecheck-client`, eslint, and `build/hygiene.ts` pass.
- **Proof** in the real Code OSS Electron window under Xvfb in a Codespace, 1600x1000 H.264 at 60fps:
  - **Copilot harness + developer mode:** step 1 highlights the model picker. Step 2 opens the menu on Agent mode with its header focused. Next collapses Agent mode, then expands Permissions. Done closes the spotlight and the menu. Telemetry shows a completed 3-step tour with no active experiment.
  - **Real ExP assignment, Chat open at startup, treatment** (signed in, temporary single-device experiment in the new workspace, on `f88b5f41a02`): the first `onb.chatInput.show` read at 1.92s is unassigned, the GitHub endpoint answers at 2.35s, the refetch reads `true` / `onb-chat-input-ab-spotlight` at 2.36s, and the tour runs without the user opening Chat. `scenarioShown` reports the active experiment and its assignment context.
  - **Real ExP assignment, Chat open at startup, control** (same setup): the first read at 1.97s is unassigned, the refetch at 2.42s reads `false` / `onb-chat-input-ab-none`, no tour shows, and telemetry carries `onb-chat-input-ab-none` from the would-show moment.
  - **Modal editor on step 3:** clicking **Configure Permissions** in the open menu opens Settings in a modal editor. The spotlight and callout end immediately, the tour stays ended after the modal closes, and `scenarioOutcome` reports `aborted` on step 3.
  - **Copilot harness, no experiment:** no tour and no tour telemetry.
  - **Local harness + developer mode:** no tour and no tour telemetry.
  - **Not run in the real window:** the separate-pickers layout. Unit tests cover it.
### Recording
Copilot harness with developer mode on `ee118845f05`, recorded at 60fps.

Scenarios.Scenario: Editor-window startup and onboarding experiment resolution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new contribution is instantiated after workbench restore, synchronously reads cached editor-chat usage, registers listeners/scenario providers, and starts asynchronous treatment reads. Workbench restoration is already complete; the assignment network fetch is owned by the pre-existing assignment service and is not introduced or awaited by this contribution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: TAS assignment initialization/refetch populates treatments; onboarding then reads the two treatment variables from the assignment client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two treatment reads per unresolved onboarding experiment; currently a small fixed set of registered onboarding scenarios. Once an experiment resolves to a valid boolean/id pair it is not read again for the window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The assignment service already initialized and fetched assignments. Before this diff, onboarding read each experiment's two treatment values once at service start; the diff adds re-reads only after an existing refetch event while unresolved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The reads are asynchronous and do not block restored workbench interaction or contribution construction. They may await assignment-client setup, but do not issue an additional fetch themselves after initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read editor chat usage counters through IStorageService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getTelemetry call per editor window contribution instantiation, reading a fixed set of usage keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This onboarding contribution and its usage read did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous cached storage access after restore; no collection-scaled disk operation is evidenced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed treatment count per registered experimental onboarding scenario and a fixed number of usage keys; no user-sized collection or request fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each experiment's two reads run in parallel. A per-scenario in-flight marker coalesces refetches to at most one follow-up read, and resolved experiments stop rereading.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Treatment reads use the assignment client's cached values after fetch; unresolved values are retried on refetch, while valid control and treatment arms are fixed for the window. Usage values come from the storage service's in-memory view.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution phase, fixed cardinality, in-flight coalescing, and assignment service call path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact assignment-client setup latency varies, but it is off the restored-workbench critical path and no new network fetch is caused by the reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added work is fixed-size, after restore, coalesced during in-flight refetches, and does not add network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: New-user Copilot harness Chat eligibility and target readiness
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When a visible eligible harness Chat exists, readiness waits one second and then resolves three DOM targets every 500 ms until all render or 40 attempts expire. This is off message-send and render critical paths, though each target visibility check synchronously reads computed style and bounds.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 40 timer attempts over about 20 seconds for one currently eligible Chat widget. Target checks short-circuit on the first missing target; successful readiness stops polling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single disposable timeout chain runs for the current eligible widget. Observable reruns dispose the prior chain when eligibility/widget identity changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used for target readiness; the ready widget is retained in an observable after success, avoiding repeat polling while the same widget remains ready.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: timer bounds, disposal ownership, and visibility helper geometry/style reads were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM dirtiness at each 500 ms check varies, but the bounded 2 Hz frequency and maximum duration are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: polling is bounded, serialized, canceled with eligibility changes, and too infrequent to establish concrete UI jank.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running the three-step Chat input spotlight tour
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The spotlight overlay and picker opening are on the tour interaction path. The overlay samples target geometry each animation frame while a step is visible; mode/permissions steps add one menu element to the sampled bounds. Section switching may pause 400 ms by design before expanding the next section.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target plus at most one additional menu element per animation frame for a single active presentation; three total tour steps and one globally serialized onboarding presentation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The onboarding presentation queue permits one active presentation. Picker handoff polling is serialized and bounded to 20 attempts at 50 ms; step cancellation stops the section-delay continuation and the overlay/listeners are disposed between steps.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No geometry cache is appropriate because target/menu positions can move. The overlay compares current and previous rectangles and only performs full layout when bounds change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: overlay animation loop, additional-element provider, picker section path, and presentation serialization were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tour dwell time is user-controlled, but per-frame cardinality remains constant and the pre-existing overlay already performed one target geometry read each frame.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds constant work for one extra element only during the rare active tour, without collection scaling or concurrent overlays.

Scenarios.Scenario: Assignment refetch while onboarding treatment reads are unresolved
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing assignment refetch event invokes onboarding experiment resolution. It reads cached post-refetch treatment variables asynchronously and reevaluates scenarios only when both values become valid; normal editor interaction does not wait for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The pre-existing TAS client performs its scheduled, filter-driven, or account-endpoint assignment fetch before emitting the refetch/update event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing assignment fetch per refetch trigger, independent of onboarding scenario count; onboarding adds no fetch per scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same assignment refetch occurred, but unresolved onboarding experiment flags were not reread afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the editor interaction critical path. Onboarding treatment reads happen after the assignment update and consume client state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of unresolved experimental onboarding scenarios; currently a small registry count, with two reads each.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reads for different unresolved scenarios can overlap; within one scenario, refetches during an in-flight read coalesce into exactly one follow-up read rather than an unbounded burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Valid assignment pairs become a positive window-lifetime cache entry. Missing/partial pairs remain negative-unresolved and are retried only on assignment refetch, with no timers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event source, local treatment read path, positive-cache lifetime, and in-flight coalescing were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future registry growth could increase local treatment reads, but current cardinality is small and each read uses the already-refetched client state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no per-scenario network fan-out is introduced, retries are event-driven and coalesced, and resolved states stop work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic onboarding run queued behind another presentation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At dequeue/presentation acquisition, the changed code rechecks context and observable eligibility before mounting UI. Ineligible automatic runs abort before presentation rendering; explicit runs retain prior behavior.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One eligibility check per dequeued automatic scenario; queue size is the small registered onboarding scenario set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single presentation queue serializes runs globally. The added check prevents stale queued work rather than adding concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Pending and inflight maps continue deduplicating runs by scenario id; no new retained cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: enqueue flags, queue pump, and presentation acquisition path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Queue contention frequency varies, but the mechanism removes stale presentation work and adds only constant predicate reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance-neutral to beneficial; this is not recorded as a regression fix because the diff and repository context do not establish a shipped performance symptom or introducing commit.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files and traced startup, treatment refetch, Chat eligibility polling, spotlight layout, picker opening/cancellation, and onboarding queue lifecycle. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and no concrete shipped performance regression fix met the blame/report threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
